label: text
text: Wong "Tso-ming, a Chinese police constable, was charged before Mr. R. E. Lindsell at the Central Magistracy this morning with misconduct as a police officer, namely 'collecting' $5.80 from

label: text

Colony on board the s.s. "Tung On." The offence was alleged to have taken place yesterday morning, at a Chinese boarding house, No. 126, Connaught Road Central.
EMPEROR'S SERIOUS CONDITION.

label: text
text: At the commencement of this morning's proceedings, His Worship asked Mr. d'Almada how his client intended pleading in answer to the charge.

label: text
text: Captain H. F. Bloxham, A.S.P., prosecuted on behalf of the Police, and Mr. Leo d'Almada defended the accused.

label: paragraph_title
text: JAPAN'S ANXIETY.

label: text
text: Mr. d'Almada: Has your Worship read the charge? I do not think that I can seriously ask my client to plead at all. He is charged with "collecting" Perhaps Captain Bloxham can explain what that means?

label: text
text: The Magistrate: I cannot refuse Mr. d'Almada's request. The defendant has only just been charged.

label: text
text:
After some discussion, His Worship ruled that the words "without authority" should be added to the charge, and Mr. d'Alemde applied for a remand.
Capt. Bloxham: I am ready to go on at once.

label: text

label: text

label: paragraph_title
text: “YOLANDA.”

label: text
text: A NATION'S PRAYERS

label: paragraph_title
text: QUEEN'S THEATRE GREAT ROMANCE

label: text
text: SPLENDID PAGEANTRY

label: text
text: A beautiful princess, a handsome prince, a stern father, a crafty king, an idiot son and a wicked ambassador—these are the central figures in "Yolanda," the film romance women round the lives of the Duke of Burgundy and Louis XI of France, now appearing at the Queen's Theatre. With such leading characters, need it be said that the story is romantic to a degree, that love, intrigue and combat a find their place and contribute towards the great climax.

label: text
text: Benides a fascinating story, "Yolanda" offers some brilliant acting, the character study of Louis XI, for one, being done with remarkable realism and penetration.

label: text
text: "Yolanda's chief claim to fame, however, is the splendour of its parceantry. The glamour of medieval court and palace is portrayed on uogigantic scale, not merely in the matter of interior settings, but in the screening of entire castles with hundreds of courtiers and men-at-arms. For these scenes alone, 'Yolanda' is one of the grandest films of medieval romance yet screened in Hong Kong.

label: paragraph_title
text: ANTI-SPANISH PLOT

label: text
text: The Catalan separatist leader, Colonel Macin, shortly after his arrival to-day from Perpignan in company with a police inspector, was confronted by Ricciotti Garibaldi, as a result of which both were arrested and sent to prison.

label: text
text: The Government has decided not only to expel Garibaldi but to proceed against him if necessary on the charge of complicity in the Catalan plot. Macla declared that Garibaldi admitted to the magistrate that he never furnished him with money or arms, and added that he has only met him once and that he recruited a certain number of Italians independently of Garibaldi.—Reuter.

label: text
text: It is noteworthy that Garibaldi is only charged in connection with the Catalan plot since his alleged activities as a secret Fascist agent presumably does not constitute an offence in French law.—Reuter.

label: text
text: Galveston, Tex., November 14.—The customs "inspectors enforcing the hitherto neglected and dense prohibition treaty seized 399 bottles of liquor on the British steamer "Asuncion Delarringa" on the ground that no intoxicants except those specified in the medical certificate might remain aboard.—Reuter's American Service.

label: paragraph_title
text: FLYING A SHORE.

label: text
text: A NOVEL PROJECT

label: text
text: Sir Alan Cobham, the famous airman, intends to carry out an interesting experiment when he leaves for "American on board the "Homeric" next Wednesday.

label: text
text: He will take with him his little moth seaplane. As the liner approaches New York, he will Tower the seaplane into the sea with a number of mail bags, and taking off from the sea, will fly with them into the city.

label: text
text: Sir Alan Cobham thinks there is a possibility of considerable acceleration of the carrying of mails in this manner.

label: text
text: He proposed to work out all the details of lifting the machines over the side to water and also to see how far it is possible to take off from the ship itself.—British Wireless Service.

label: paragraph_title
text: BY AIR TO INDIA.

label: text
text: EARL WINTERTON ON FUTURE DEVELOPMENTS.

label: text
text: London, October 29.—Earl Winterton in a statement to the Imperial Conference on October 28 said that there was no need to stress the importance of air communication between India and other parts of the Empire. India had a far larger population than all the rest of the Empire combined. She was the largest individual customer of Great Britain.

label: text
text: Since direct rail communication between India and Great Britain was ruled out owing to the present state of the world for many years to come, perhaps for all time, the air afforded the only alternative, supplementing and extending the present traffic by sea in persons and goods.

label: text
text: There could be no doubt that India was destined to play a prominent part in the development of air communications between countries of the Empire.

label: text
text: Any service between Europe and the Far East or Australia would en its way have to cross India.

label: text
text: It was reasonable to anticipate a function of these two routes which would almost inevitably be on Indian soil and ultimately would figure as one of the most vital points in the Empire chain.

label: paragraph_title
text: BRAKE FOR AEROPLANES.

label: text
text: London, October 26.—Mechanism for providing aeroplanes with a touch needed brake was described by Mr. G. H. Dowty in a lecture at the Institution of Aeronautical Engineers. This consisted of a drum carrying a cable with an anchor fixed at the outer end. The anchor would be lowered on landing and engage a series of cross ropes, while the unwinding of the cable would cause the drum to rotate and operate the mechanism for obtaining the uniform resistance which would permit aircraft landing at 90 miles an hour to come steadily to rest within 200 feet, namely, half the length provided on landing decks.—"Times of Ceylon"

label: paragraph_title
text: 60th BIRTHDAY.

label: paragraph_title
text: THE LATE DR. SUN YAT SEN'S MEMORY

label: text
text: Carlton, Nov. 13.

label: text
text: One of the biggest popular celebrations ever held in China was the Canton commemoration of the 60th birthday of Dr. Sun Yat-sen held yesterday. A conservative estimate places the number of people attending the various exercises at over 500,000.

label: text
text: All but necessary work was stopped while the city threw itself into an ardent manifestation of love for the late leader of the Nationalist movement and a determination to bring his dreams of a united and free China to realisation.

label: text
text: The celebration began with a monster lantern procession on the evening of Thursday. The number of paraders was over 200,000 comprising members of the labour unions, student bodies, peasants, and the official and merchant bodies.

label: text
text:
Streets Blocked 4 Hours.
Traffic was blocked in all streets for over four hours while the singing, shouting paraders marched through the entire city.

label: text
text: The formal celebration of the birthday took place on the East Parade ground at noon yesterday with speakers addressing crowds totalling over 150,000 from five platforms. The speakers on the main platform included Mr. Ku Mang-yu and Mr. Sun Fo (Nationalist Ministers).

label: text
text: Simultaneously hundreds of speakers from specially erected platforms throughout the city addressed street crowds while the processions were constantly moving about the city.

label: text
text: Madame Sun Yat-sen spoke before an indoor meeting at Chungshan University on the character of her late husband.—Canton Bureau of Information through Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: VOICE FROM GRAVE

label: text
text:
WOMAN WHO WAS BURIED
ALIVE

label: text
text: Pekin, October 28.—A traveller just arriving at Peking from Yungching, Chihli, states that in the village of Heiwu in that district a young lady about twenty years of age who had been ill for a number of days passed away and was buried at once.

label: text
text: Three days after her death, according to custom, her mother-in-law went to her tomb to perform sucrificial ceremony by burning paper money. To her great astonishment, she heard cries from inside the grave and a voice which seemed to say.

label: text
text: "Your daughter-in-law is alive, pray be not terrified."

label: text
text: Upon this, the mother-in-law at once returned home where she assembled a dozen of brave men, who took with them shovels and axles. On arriving at the grave they tore it down and found the buried woman alive. She was so weak that she could not move. She was carried home, and still lives.—"Chung Mei."

label: paragraph_title
text: GERMAN POLITICS.

label: text
text: Berlin, October 28.—Speaking at a meeting of the German National People's Party at Leipzig, Count Westarp, the noted leader of the Party, stressed the impossibility of his Party's co-operation with the Social-Democratic Party, which, although not represented in the Reichs-government, is co-operating with it at least as far as its foreign policy is concerned.

label: text
text: Count Westarp further said that the Reich-government would have to choose between the two parties, inasmuch as the present opportunism of the Catholic Centre Party, which in the Reichs-government maintains a coalition with the German People's Party and the Democratic Party, and in Prussia with the Democrats and the Social-Democratic Party, could not be maintained indefinitely.

The young couple remained quiet and, having no money, handed over the jewellery in the girl's possession, consisting of a pair of ear-rings and a ring. As the transaction was taking place, the young man suddenly seized the prisoner and a struggle ensued, lasting for ten minutes or so, in the course of which the pistol was dropped and the girl picked it up, finding that it was a toy.

label: text
text: Throughout the struggle, the girl had been screaming for help. Hearing her cries, Messrs. H. Owen Hughes and A. J. Hazeland, who were walking in May Road, ran down the steps in the vicinity and, on arriving at the spot, were able to overpower the prisoner with whom the young man was still struggling.

label: text
text: The prisoner had evidently concealed the articles of jewellery with some "ingenuity," said Mr. Dyer Ball, as they were not found on his person for some time after his arrest.

label: text
text: His Lordship asked that the young man who had struggled with the prisoner might be rought into court.

label: text
text: After ascertaining that neither he nor the lady had suffered injury as a result of the struggle, His Lordship said he wished to express his appreciation of the young man's conduct. He had conducted himself with considerable gallantry in tackling a man whom he had every reason to believe held a loaded revolver. The conduct of the two European gentlemen had also been commendable.

label: text
text: Addressing Mr. Owen Hughes in person, His Lordship said that he wished on behalf of the public, to express his appreciation of the conduct of all parties in the case. If more members of the public behaved as the young man had done there would be fewer of these cases.

label: text
text: Addressing the prisoner, the Chief Justice said that he had pleaded guilty to a serious "offence which was getting & great deal too common in the Colony. In sentencing prisoner he would take into consideration the fact that he had not caused injury to those he had tried to rob. He would, however "have to make the sentence severe to make people like prisoner think before they attempted such acts. Although the pistol used was a toy, it had every appearance of being the real thing and had been used with the intention of terrifying his would-be victims. The fact that prisoner had pleaded guilty and that the revolver was not actually a serviceable one had been taken into consideration. The sentence of the court would be three years' imprisonment.

label: paragraph_title
text: TOLSTO'S SON.

label: text
text: PROPHESIES THE OVERTHROW OF THE SOVIET.

label: text
text: The Russian peasant will rise and overthrow Bolshevist rule in Russia, declared. Count Ilya Tolstoi, son of the late Count Leo Tolstoi, in an interview at Los Angeles, states the "Evening Standard."

label: text
text: Count Tolstoi and his wife are now" in Southern California to supervise the film production of "Resurrection," his father's famous novel.

label: text
text: Bolshevist rule to-day is minority rule," said Count Tolstoi. "As a natural sequence in the development of Russia the peasants will overthrow the Soviet. To-day the peasants are not conscious of their strength. When they do realise their power they will revolt and there will be a real Russian republic," he declared.

label: paragraph_title
text: TWO NIGHTS' JAIL.

label: text
text: "You have been locked up for two nights; you can go. Don't do it again," said Mr. R. E. Lindsell to a Chinese coolie charged at the Central Magistracy this morning, with smoking opium. Six others caught at the same time failed to put in an appearance, the Magistrate ordering their bail, $3 each, to be estreated. The principal tenant of the premises was fined $100 or two months.

label: paragraph_title
text: DARING BANDITS

label: text
text: The wireless has picked up a report that bandits on Thursday fired on and captured an American vessel and a Chinese tug and junk near Chenglin, near Changsha. The bandits demanded ransom, but the vessel was released on Thursday night. There are no details. —Reuter
